## 1.) Define Kmer using your own words ##
Kmers are sequences, usually overlapping, and of a fixed length "k". They are used to efficiently analyze genomic data and error correction.

## 2.) Define N50 and L90 using your own words ##
N50 is the shortest contig/scaffold length when 50% of the total assembly length is covered. When 50% is covered, the length that covers the half-way point is your N50 number. L90 is the minimum number of contigs/scaffolds whose length adds up to 90% of the assembly length. We want to have a high N50 and a low L90. 

## 3.) Based on your results and the table you filled, what is the best K-mer value? ##
Based on the table, we believe a K-value of 121 would be best. This is based on the fact that K-121 has the highest N50 value (692) and lowest number of scaffolds (2004).

## 4.) What was the best K-mer value selected by Unicycler? ##
Unicycler selected 93 as the best K-mer value.

## 5.) What assembly was better? Any of the SPADES assemblies or the Unicycler? ##
Based on the assemblies from SPADES and Unicycler, the best assembly is the one generated by Unicycler. We base this off the fact that K=93, which was selected by Unicycler, has the highest N50, lowest L90, and least number of scaffolds, telling us this is the best assembly to use.

## 7.) What are the GENUS with higher WKID scores? ##
Based on the result of the Sketch, the genus with the higher WKID scores and have the most hits are Synechococcus sp. and filamentous cyanobacteria.

## 8.) What is the WKID score of your assembly when compared to Synechococcus? ##
The WKID score of cyanobacteria is 0.04, the same score as Synechococcus. 

## 9.) Summarize your results and what they mean ##
There is not a significant amount of cyanobacteria, of which the amount of WKID score is 0.04, the same as Synechococcus. This means that there is alot of contamination in the sample.

## 10.) What blast program are we using and what does it mean? What is the nt database? ##
The program we are using is called Blobtools, which determines the taxonomic assignment and the coverage for every single scaffold in the assembly. The "nt" database is the NCBI's nucleotide database, which the blobtools will compare against.

## 11.) What do the -max_target_seqs and -max_hsps flags mean? ##
The "-max_target_seqs" option means that any BLAST hits that are above the e-value cutoff are presented.
The "-max_hsps" is the maximum number of alignments to keep.

## 12.) What is the e-value used as threshold? What does e-value mean? ##
The usual e-value used as the threshold is 10.0, which is the expected value for saving hits.
